verdict.rationale: ROS 2's documented model of drivers publishing standardized message types over topics gives application code a stable interface to code against, so a sensor can be swapped by replacing the driver node. Topics are documented for streaming sensor data (ros2-docs-45), static name remapping is supported (ros2-docs-31), and the project positions itself as spanning 'drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms' (ros2-gh-1). A community user confirms that shared message definitions let components interoperate without constant glue code (ros2-comm-19). However, the evidence never describes a dedicated hardware-abstraction layer or a documented driver-swap workflow, and actuator abstraction is not covered at all. missing for 10: an explicit hardware-abstraction/controller interface for actuators, first-party docs on swapping hardware without code changes, standardized sensor/actuator interface definitions, and hands-on corroboration of real hardware swaps.
